prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: rear-end collision in Pearland, Texas. Injury: neck and back strain. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1210; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record, so you can just refer to me as the plaintiff.

Q: Do you understand that you are under oath today?
A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Where were you on the day of the collision?
A: I was driving home from work on a county road near Pearland, Texas, in the right lane. It was late afternoon and traffic had slowed down ahead of me.

Q: Describe what happened when the collision occurred.
A: I had stopped behind a sedan at a red light. I looked in my mirror and saw a pickup coming fast. I had just enough time to brace myself before it hit the back of my car. My head snapped forward and then back against the headrest.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?
A: Yes, I was.

Q: Did you get out of the vehicle at the scene?
A: I got out, but I felt dizzy and sore, so I sat on the curb until the police and an ambulance arrived.

Q: Did you go to the hospital that day?
A: Yes, I was taken by ambulance to the emergency room. They took X-rays and gave me a muscle relaxer, then sent me home.

Q: What treatment have you received since the collision?
A: I've been going to physical therapy about three times a week. I also see my family doctor regularly, and I had a few sessions with a chiropractor. I still do stretching exercises at home every morning.

Q: Describe your neck and back symptoms today.
A: My neck is stiff, especially when I turn to check my blind spot while driving. My lower back aches if I sit for more than an hour, and sometimes I get a sharp pain down my left leg.

Q: How has the collision affected your work?
A: I'm a warehouse supervisor, and I've had to miss several shifts. I can't lift boxes like I used to, so I've been reassigned to desk duties for now.

Q: How has it changed your daily activities?
A: I used to coach my son's soccer team and go hiking on weekends. I've stopped both. Simple things like carrying groceries or sleeping through the night are harder now.

Q: Before this collision, had you ever injured your neck or back?
A: No, not that I can recall. I had no treatment for my neck or back before this.

Q: Is there anything else about the collision or your injuries you'd like to add?
A: Only that I want to get back to normal. I'm working hard at therapy, and I hope to return to full duty soon.
